title: Equal spatial gradients and equal total turnover can give different thermal tracking in a four-state community model
abstract: We ask if total species turnover can exclude a long thermal lag. We construct two reversible four-state community models with the same spatial equilibrium distribution at every temperature and the same total baseline turnover at every time lag. Their small-signal endpoint responses to a 30-year warming ramp are 0.120 and 0.967 of their common spatial expectation. Independent replication of occupied slots extends the result to fixed-richness communities. Thus unmarked turnover and spatial distributions do not identify thermal tracking. We apply a known Markov response identity to give a conditional test based on independent baseline records and a spatial temperature score. In an aligned reversible case, thermal autocorrelation gives finite-window bounds. Five years of exact memory give bounds of 0.039-0.837 in the slow example and 0.961-0.967 in the fast example. Score mismatch and measurement noise can invalidate a naive CTI autocorrelation test. Algebra, matrix exponentials and forward integration check the results. These are synthetic counterexamples and a methods result, not field estimates or proof of a cause of the observed gap.

display.caption: Synthetic models have identical total turnover but different thermal memory and ramp response. Independent measurement noise can hide long memory.
